entries: Clipping of Bundesfreiwilligendienstleistender + -i, based on Zivi.

From Middle High German būhurt, bēhurt, or Middle Low German bohurt, burt, later the term for a ”tournament-melee”, a medieval tournament game, in which mock combat is conducted between two groups of knights, alternatively a game in which an attack was made on a pretend fortress, but also a synonym for tournament in general.
Cognates includes Old Italian bohordicum; English bohort; French bohourt (Old French behort, bohort, bohourt, bouhourd); Swedish bohord (Old Swedish bohordh, behordh); Icelandic burt (Old Norse burt). Also compare the verbal form (“to bohort”): Middle High German buhurdieren, buhurtieren; Old French behorder, bohorder, bouhourder, buhourder; Middle Low German borderen; Swedish bordera (Old Swedish bordera).
senses: a medieval tournament game: bohort, melee
a hastilude of the 12th and 13th centuries, involving horse-riding, lance play, and clashing of shields

entries: From Kaiser (“emperor”) + Wetter (“weather”). Originally referred to the notion that the weather was usually sunny on the birthday of Austrian Emperor Franz Joseph I (reigned 1848–1916). senses: clear, sunny weather, usually with pleasant temperatures, and especially when there is some event
